acceptance.given: Package A is validated against the declared policy and schemas using the repository-local validator entry point.

oracle.expected: The standard, versioned policy and schemas define package declaration and structure checks; validate_package and its CLI return the documented versioned result shape with authorizes=[] and do not execute package commands or grant runtime permissions.
forbidden: Validator execution of a Skill or package-declared command
Validator claim of runtime security or product acceptance
Raw package content, secret values, or absolute host paths in diagnostics
oracle.observable: A structured validator result and published standard/schema artifacts are inspected during the validation run.

acceptance.then: The capability-aware standard and read-only validator are implemented within their declared authority.
acceptance.when: Run the validator and inspect its standard, policy, schemas, callable validate_package API, and CLI result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A declared Package A validator test invokes validate_package or the published CLI and fails when package declaration/structure checks or the authorizes=[] authority boundary is absent.

affected_subjects: Capability-aware authoring standard and package validator
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add the capability-aware Package A authoring policy and read-only package validator with a callable API and JSON CLI contract.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Remove the Package A validator artifacts while preserving existing skill-contract and skill-input protocols; no live data migration is required.

slice_hint.state_transition: No established Package A validator -> published standard/policy/schemas and read-only validator available for local package checks.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The four declared Package A pytest modules pass and the real CLI returns the documented structured result for a reference package without execution authority.

acceptance.given: Declared Package A cases and documentary constraints are authored against the real production validator contract.

oracle.expected: Each executable case calls validate_package or the published CLI with a literal argv list; documentary constraints have explicit artifact or contract assertions and use a non-RED failure role; no case substitutes a mock product implementation.
forbidden: Mock or replacement validator used instead of the real API or CLI
Documentary constraint without an explicit assertion
Product RED classification for a non-executable documentary constraint
oracle.observable: Test source and contract assertions are inspected, and the terminal integration case records the real entry-point invocation and structured checks.

acceptance.then: Behavioral and documentary obligations have suitable test or contract oracles and failure roles.
acceptance.when: Review and execute the declared Package A case modules, including the terminal integration case.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The declared case and documentary-contract checks fail when a test uses a mock, omits an explicit assertion, or assigns product RED to a documentary constraint.

affected_subjects: Real production cases and documentary checks

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Test and fixture additions are disposable; existing validator protocols remain unchanged.

slice_hint.state_transition: Undeclared or mock-based cases -> real-entry tests with explicit documentary assertions and classified non-RED failures.

acceptance.given: The Package A test suite contains positive and negative cases that exercise real validator behavior and structured diagnostics.

forbidden: Unconditional-pass validator satisfies the complete Package A test suite
Tests that only observe process exit 0, file existence, or a status string without semantic checks

acceptance.then: Tests distinguish real validation behavior from an unconditional pass implementation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The Package A test selectors must fail when validate_package is replaced by an unconditional pass result, demonstrating nontrivial semantic or boundary assertions.
